findings.summary: dependents_unnamed would ship as a public admission function that only the replay test calls, and it judges 'named' by substring match, so criterion 2 mostly tests the test's own helper.
findings.evidence: The plan says plan_findings will not call the helper (decision 4) and production never runs the search (criterion 2 seam). The helper counts a path as named when any entry's name, dependent, test or reason contains the path or its file name. An entry that mentions 'verify.rs' while saying something unrelated would therefore count as naming the seen-commands rule. Nothing in the shipped admission path enforces that verify.rs is named. Fix: Keep the helper in the test module (cfg(test)) or in refusal_corpus.rs instead of as public admission code, so admission does not ship an unused heuristic. Keep the docs/CHANGELOG sentence saying the CI-reuse search is a replay test plus a prompt rule, not a production check.

findings.summary: The 15% figure is about readings, but this rule refuses plans; the changelog should not imply the share was measured.
findings.evidence: The rule runs in plan_findings, on plans. The reading's figure is 'expected 15% of newly refused readings', and nothing measures it. replay_declaration in reading.rs parses such shares from criterion text for reading checks only. Fix: In the changelog and the case notes, label 15% as an estimate taken from the reading and say these are plans newly refused, not readings.

summary: The plan matches the reading. I checked it by reading and searching the code, and ran no tests. plan_findings is at admission.rs:166. In planning.rs (lines 212-239), a Major finding from Athena's own checks sends the plan back to the planner with no critic call, up to MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES, so the choice of a revisable Major finding over a hard serde failure is sound. verify.rs:378 has the filter `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()`, so the replay test's source check has something real to match. The schema test's nested-object count is 5 today (outputs.rs:669), so 5 to 6 is right. The search for scripted plan JSON and JobPlan literals ("risks", "demonstrations", "JobPlan {") finds exactly the 14 files the plan lists, so fixture coverage is complete. The changelog test only requires certain phrases in CHANGELOG.md, so a new entry cannot break it. Using serde default plus skip-if-empty on JobPlan, and printing the Dependents block only when non-empty, keeps old record bytes and plan hashes. The demonstrations for criteria 1, 3, 6 and 8 call real entry points (plan_findings, plan_schema, AnyRecord::parse, check_budget) and would fail without the change. The one weak spot is criterion 2: its helper is used only by the test and matches by substring. The plan says this openly and the out-of-scope list forbids static analysis, so it is a minor finding.
